questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the main ore of iron?
questions.explanation: Hematite is the main ore of iron. Iron can be extracted from this ore.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which metal is found in pure state in nature?
questions.explanation: Gold is very less reactive. So it can be found in pure state in nature.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the primary step of purifying metal?
questions.explanation: Concentration removes unwanted impurities from ore first. So it is the primary step in metal purification.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following ore is oxidised by roasting method?
questions.explanation: Cuprite can be changed into oxide by roasting. Roasting means heating the ore in air.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In which process is smelting included?
questions.explanation: Smelting helps remove oxygen from metal oxide. So it is included in reduction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a naturally occurring source from which useful metals may be obtained called?
questions.explanation: A mineral is a natural material found in Earth. Useful metals can be obtained from some minerals.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is an ore?
options: A mineral from which metal can be extracted economically
questions.explanation: An ore is a useful mineral. Metal can be extracted from it economically.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which ore is associated with aluminium in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Bauxite is the ore of aluminium. Aluminium is extracted from bauxite.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which ore is associated with silver in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Argentite is the ore of silver. So it is associated with silver.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the name of the process of extracting metal from its ore?
questions.explanation: Metallurgy means extracting metals from ores. It includes concentration, reduction and refining.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which step removes unwanted impurities from an ore before further treatment?
questions.explanation: Concentration removes gangue from ore. This makes the ore better for the next steps.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What are unwanted impurities in ore commonly removed during concentration?
questions.explanation: Gangue or matrix means unwanted impurities in ore. These impurities are removed during concentration.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is roasting?
options: Heating ore in no air only
Heating ore in presence of air
questions.explanation: Roasting means heating ore in air. It is commonly used for sulphide ores.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is calcination?
options: Heating ore in limited or no air
questions.explanation: Calcination means heating ore in little or no air. It is commonly used for carbonate ores.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which process is used to obtain pure copper from impure copper in the activity?
questions.explanation: Electro-refining purifies impure copper. Pure copper gets deposited on the cathode.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which solution is used as electrolyte in copper electro-refining activity?
questions.explanation: Copper sulphate solution carries copper ions. So it works as the electrolyte.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In copper electro-refining, the impure copper plate is connected as what?
questions.explanation: In copper electro-refining, impure copper is connected to the positive terminal. So it acts as the anode.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In copper electro-refining, the pure copper plate is connected as what?
questions.explanation: Pure copper plate is connected to the negative terminal. So it acts as the cathode.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to the impure copper anode during electro-refining?
questions.explanation: Copper from the impure anode goes into solution. So the anode slowly erodes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where does pure copper deposit during electro-refining?
questions.explanation: Copper ions move to the cathode. So pure copper deposits on the cathode.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are all ores minerals but all minerals are not ores?
options: Only some minerals contain enough metal for economical extraction.
questions.explanation: All ores are minerals because they come from natural minerals. But only useful and economical minerals are called ores.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches ore and metal?
questions.explanation: Hematite contains iron. So the correct pair is hematite and iron.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches ore and metal?
questions.explanation: Bauxite contains aluminium. So the correct pair is bauxite and aluminium.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches ore and metal?
questions.explanation: Argentite contains silver. So the correct pair is argentite and silver.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which process changes sulphide ore into oxide by heating in air?
questions.explanation: Roasting heats sulphide ore in air. This changes it into oxide ore.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which process is generally applied to carbonate ore to change it into oxide?
questions.explanation: Calcination heats carbonate ore in limited air. This changes carbonate ore into oxide.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which step follows concentration when ores are converted into oxide form?
questions.explanation: After concentration, ore is changed into oxide form. This step is called oxidation.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is reduction important in metallurgy?
options: It helps obtain metal from its oxide.
questions.explanation: Reduction removes oxygen from metal oxide. This helps get the metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best describes smelting?
options: A reduction process used to obtain metal from oxide ore
questions.explanation: Smelting is a reduction process. It helps obtain metal from its oxide ore.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the correct order of broad metallurgical steps?
questions.explanation: Ore is first concentrated, then oxidised, then reduced. Finally the metal is refined to make it pure.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which process improves the purity of metal after extraction?
questions.explanation: Refining removes remaining impurities from metal. So it improves metal purity.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is electrolysis useful in refining copper?
options: It transfers pure copper onto the cathode from solution.
questions.explanation: During electrolysis, copper ions deposit on the cathode. This gives pure copper.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which item is required in the electro-refining activity?
questions.explanation: A battery supplies electric current. Current is needed for electro-refining.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In the electro-refining setup, which electrode gains pure copper?
questions.explanation: The cathode gets copper ions from the solution. So pure copper deposits on the cathode.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the role of copper sulphate solution in electro-refining?
options: It acts as a food preservative.
It acts as dry lime tower.
questions.explanation: Copper sulphate solution lets copper ions move. So it acts as the electrolyte.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes mineral and ore?
options: Ore is always detergent; mineral is soap.
Ore contains no metal; mineral always contains gold.
Ore is a useful mineral for extracting metal; mineral may or may not be useful as an ore.
questions.explanation: Ore is a mineral useful for metal extraction. A mineral may not have enough metal to be an ore.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes roasting and calcination?
options: Roasting is heating in air; calcination is heating in limited or no air.
Roasting is ripening fruit; calcination is making alcohol.
questions.explanation: Roasting is heating in air. Calcination is heating in limited or no air.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes oxidation and reduction in metallurgy?
options: Oxidation converts ore to oxide; reduction obtains metal from oxide.
Oxidation deposits copper on cathode; reduction makes detergent.
questions.explanation: Oxidation changes ore into oxide. Reduction changes metal oxide into metal.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which metal is mentioned as occurring in pure state because of low reactivity?
questions.explanation: Gold is less reactive than many metals. So it can stay pure in nature.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is metallurgy described as stepwise?
options: All metals are extracted in one single step without change.
It is only a diagram activity.
Each stage prepares ore or metal for the next stage of extraction and purification.
questions.explanation: Metallurgy has many steps because ore contains impurities. Each step prepares it for the next step.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A student connects impure copper to the positive terminal and pure copper to the negative terminal in copper sulphate solution. What process is being demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Impure copper as anode and pure copper as cathode show electro-refining. Copper gets purified by electric current.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If an ore is first concentrated, then converted into oxide and finally reduced, which topic is being described?
questions.explanation: These are the main steps of metallurgy. They help extract metal from ore.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which electrode pair is correct for copper electro-refining?
options: Pure copper - anode; impure copper - cathode
Impure copper - anode; pure copper - cathode
questions.explanation: Impure copper is connected as anode. Pure copper is connected as cathode.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which observation proves electro-refining of copper is occurring?
options: Fruit ripens due to calcium carbide.
Impure anode erodes and pure copper deposits on cathode.
questions.explanation: The impure anode becomes smaller. Pure copper deposits on the cathode, showing electro-refining.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is concentration done before oxidation and reduction?
options: It removes gangue so later extraction steps become more effective.
It makes the ore a detergent.
questions.explanation: Concentration removes gangue first. Then oxidation and reduction become easier and better.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which ore-treatment pair is most suitable from the chapter idea?
questions.explanation: Carbonate ores are changed into oxides by calcination. So carbonate ore and calcination match.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A mineral contains metal but extraction is not economical. How should it be classified?
questions.explanation: It is a mineral because it contains metal. It is not an ore because extraction is not economical.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which answer best explains why gold can be found in a pure state?
options: It is less reactive than many other metals.
questions.explanation: Gold is less reactive. So it does not easily form compounds and can remain pure.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which broad process includes smelting and helps obtain metal from oxide?
questions.explanation: Reduction removes oxygen from oxide ore. Smelting is a reduction process.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which conclusion is drawn in the copper purification activity?
options: Pure copper can be obtained from impure copper by electrolysis.
Copper sulphate is a food preservative.
questions.explanation: Electrolysis can purify copper. Pure copper is obtained from impure copper in electro-refining.
